papers.title: Anomaly Detection of Tabular Data Using LLMs
papers.authors: Aodong Li, Yunhan Zhao, Chen Qiu
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown their potential in long-context understanding and mathematical reasoning. In this paper, we study the problem of using LLMs to detect tabular anomalies and show that pre-trained LLMs are zero-shot batch-level anomaly detectors. That is, without extra distribution-specific model fitting, they can discover hidden outliers in a batch of data, demonstrating their ability to identify low-density data regions. papers.title: Maximally Divergent Intervals for Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Erik Rodner, Björn Barz, Yanira Guanche
papers.abstract: We present new methods for batch anomaly detection in multivariate time series. Our methods are based on maximizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the data distribution within and outside an interval of the time series. An empirical analysis shows the benefits of our algorithms compared to methods that treat each time step independently from each other without optimizing with respect to all possible intervals.

papers.title: Trustworthy Anomaly Detection: A Survey
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection has a wide range of real-world applications, such as bank fraud detection and cyber intrusion detection. In the past decade, a variety of anomaly detection models have been developed, which lead to big progress towards accurately detecting various anomalies. Despite the successes, anomaly detection models still face many limitations. The most significant one is whether we can trust the detection results from the models. candidate_claims.description: Paper proposes serializing tabular data to text and prompting LLMs for zero-shot batch-level anomaly detection, with fine-tuning via synthetic Gaussian/categorical mixtures. Benchmarks on ODDS (27 datasets) show GPT-4 achieves AUROC parity with KNN/ECOD baselines; Llama2/Mistral improve significantly post-fine-tuning. Addresses detection in numerical tables and output parsing. Directly relevant to anomaly detection methods but lacks domain constraints or problem-specific calibration. No treatment of convergence metrics or diminishing returns in detection performance.
